summary.oneLiner: Solarium delivered strong H1FY26 growth (43% revenue, 36% EBITDA) despite monsoon and GST 2.0 delays, with a pivotal 1GW module plant commissioning by mid-January 2026 set to drive 5-7% gross margin expansion via captive consumption and cost advantage, transforming its EPC model into a vertically integrated player.

one-line thesis: Solarium delivered strong H1FY26 growth (43% revenue, 36% EBITDA) despite monsoon and GST 2.0 delays, with a pivotal 1GW module plant commissioning by mid-January 2026 set to drive 5-7% gross margin expansion via captive consumption and cost advantage, transforming its EPC model into a vertically integrated player.
financial scorecard: revenue: +43% YoY; EBITDA: +36% YoY; margin: expanded due to structure cost savings (0.3-0.5% EPC impact); PAT: +22% YoY (normalized: higher due to one-off defense receivable delays); order book: INR229cr unexecuted + INR209cr L1 + INR900cr pipeline; net debt: elevated due to defense receivables (INR20-25cr recovered Oct-Sep, fully cleared by Dec 2025)
guidance: revenue growth: sustained EPC momentum (past 4x growth in 2 yrs); margin: 5-7% gross margin uplift from module captive use; order inflow: INR900cr pipeline; capex/commissioning: 1GW module plant commissioned by mid-Jan 2026
order book & pipeline: INR229cr unexecuted (target completion by Q1FY27); INR209cr L1 (execution in 9-12m post-LOA); INR900cr bidding pipeline (mostly non-defense: NTPC, HPPL)
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: 32% revenue, expanded to 25+ cities via 450+ Solarium Saarthi franchisees; Government: 36% revenue, driven by NTPC/HPPL (defense delays were one-off); B2B Module Sales: emerging from Jan 2026; Trading: 70% of distribution segment (negative WC, low-margin)
growth verticals / optionality: 1GW module plant enables captive supply (50%+ consumption target), B2C app for customer retention, BESS EPC bids active (no BESS manufacturing), franchisee network scaling
margins & cost dynamics: Structure manufacturing: 5% cost advantage → 0.3-0.5% EPC margin uplift; Module manufacturing: 12-13% standalone EBITDA margin; 5-7% gross margin uplift expected from captive consumption (modules = 50% of EPC cost); GST 2.0 cut to 5% boosts demand
capex / expansion: 1GW automated module plant commissioned by mid-Jan 2026; structure plant already operational; no new capex announced beyond this
capital allocation: IPO proceeds held as buffer for manufacturing WC (INR60-70cr needed in Q4); debt used for plant financing; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on balanced debt-equity
risks & watch-items: Defense receivables volatility (one-off resolved); module plant ramp-up risk (target 75% util by Q2FY27); competition from unorganized installers (96% market); DCR compliance post-June 2026 (plant capable); working capital pressure during ramp-up
management quality / tone: Confident, transparent, and execution-focused; acknowledged one-offs (defense delays, GST slowdown); emphasized vertical integration as core strategy; no formal guidance but clear targets on utilization and margin uplift
non-obvious takeaways: Franchisee model (Solarium Saarthi) reduces capex risk while scaling reach; B2C app is CX tool, not revenue stream; trading segment (70% of distribution) is negative WC, subsidizing core EPC; defense delays were tied to Operation Sindoor (India-Pakistan conflict), not systemic

scorecard.wc_basis: neutral (needs 2 FYs of BS_Working capital; real from FY27)
scorecard.piotroski_basis: needs 2 FYs of BS_* -> 0 (real from FY27)
scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)
scorecard.notes: growth: insufficient history; cfo/pat over 1y only; share cagr: n/a; promoter: no SHP row
